messages:
Jordan: Quick heads-up — after last night's deploy we saw a throughput regression on Mixtral-8B hosted endpoints. p50 latency ~+8%, p95 ~+12%. Repro with our standard chat template (system + user) and wide variance in token counts per request.

Anya: Ugh. Any profiler traces?

Jordan: Yep, attaching a short flame output from the runtime profiler:

```
PROFILE SAMPLE (mixtral-8b @ seq=1024)
kernel_select: conv_gemm_fp16  38.2ms
kernel_select: attn_kv_gather   12.4ms
kv_cache_update:             15.7ms
batch_dispatch_overhead:     22.8ms
network_wait:                 3.1ms
TOTAL per-token:              91.2ms
```

Jordan: Note batch_dispatch_overhead spiked vs baseline (was ~8ms). Also seeing many tiny batches (few tokens) causing poor kernel packing.

Mike: Two quick hypotheses: (1) tokenizer byte-fallback is creating more tokens for some user strings (emoji + non-norm chars) so requests that used to be 40 tokens are now 70 — batches misalign. (2) RoPE scaling differences between our Mixtral/KV code path vs model-compiled config cause invalid cache reuse and extra KV updates.

Anya: I dug into request traces. Example: same message, two paths:
- client A (no normalization): 38 tokens, single chunk batch
- client B (emoji sequence -> byte fallback): 72 tokens, gets split, ends up as two small batches and forces KV cache evictions mid-request.

Sam: Can you paste the exact tokenizer config we pushed? IIRC we flipped on byte_fallback fallback to handle malformed utf-8 earlier.

Jordan: Current runtime tokenizer config:

```
{
  "tokenizer": {
    "normalize": "",
    "byte_fallback": true,
    "add_bos": true,
    "preserve_eos": false
  }
}
```

Anya: That's the culprit. Byte fallback = true is good for robustness but raises token counts dramatically for some inputs. That combined with our batching heuristic (align_by_request_count) produces lots of small batches.

Mike: About RoPE: when we switched to the optimized attention kernel we added a tiny scale factor (rope_alpha = 1.03) to match quantized weights. That breaks positional caching equivalence across cached vs new requests — keys differ and we can't reuse slices, so kv_cache_update becomes expensive.

Sam: So two-pronged fix: normalize inputs and change batching heuristics to prefer token-aligned groups, plus revert the rope_alpha tweak until we can ensure kernel-level equivalence.

Anya: Proposed quick change (hotfix):

```
# runtime config patch
"tokenizer": {"normalize":"NFKC","byte_fallback":false,"add_bos":false},
"batching": {"strategy":"token_aligned","max_tokens_per_batch":4096,"min_requests_for_batch":2},
"kernel": {"rope_scale_override":null}
```

Mike: Also add a runtime telemetry gate that emits: tokens_before_tokenizer_norm / tokens_after_norm and a small histo of token_count_delta per request so we can confirm delta goes down.

Jordan: I can roll that patch to staging now. Two questions: will disabling add_bos break any downstream evals or parsing? Some chat templates explicitly expect a single BOS token.

Anya: We should preserve logical separation: keep add_bos disabled at runtime for hosted endpoints and have an opt-in flag for client libraries that need explicit BOS. We'll update SDKs.

infra-bot: Deploy job #deploy-1765432115 created by jordan -> staging. CI: unit tests passed, smoke tests queued. :rocket:

Mike: One more small perf note: set kernel preference to prefer_fast_gemm for short sequences, and keep int8_fallback but disable fallback after 8 tokens. That reduces conv_gemm_fp16->fallback churn per token.

Sam: I'll add a tiny change to allocator heuristics to avoid KV evictions on split batches: bump per-request kv_reserve_ratio to 1.2 for Mixtral-8B. That should reduce eviction thrash while we validate rope_scale fix.

Jordan: Plan: (1) rollout tokenizer + batching patch to staging (done), (2) monitor p50/p95 and tiny-batch histogram for 4h, (3) if good, push to prod with a canary, (4) revert rope_alpha tweak in model-kernel mapping and schedule follow-up work to re-evaluate quantization alignment.

Anya: I'll own the telemetry dashboards and add the token-delta widget + tiny-batch rate.

Jordan: Thanks all. If staging looks stable I'll open a short RFC for the rope scaling behavior so the team can review the kernel changes vs model metadata.

Sam: TL;DR: byte_fallback + rope_alpha change = KV-cache blasting + dispatch overhead. Hotfix is tokenizer normalization + token_aligned batching + reserve bump. :thumbsup:
